original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Finite verification inside the masked (E-graph) model: for every 5-subset and every 6-subset X of P112 (1614 and 19295 orbits under the 8-generator FRAME0-stabiliser subgroup, covered by explicit generator words), is there a pivot frame F inside P112 \ X satisfying PR1560's frame-incidence criterion (D), (G), (W) and the nonempty-block premise of its Corollary 2? If so, PR1560's written theorem makes every P107 and P106 unit rigid.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a masked decoder can beat the floor. The rank-8 line (PR1212, PR1399, PR1419, PR1474, PR1568) answers it for exactly eight costly terms down to P108 and reduced P107 to zero exclusion. an664's PR1560 then gave a structural criterion whose Corollary 2 implies rigidity directly; this package checks its finite premises on every P107 and P106 unit, answering PR1560's open question. It constructs no decoder.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the binding complex supplier: with PR1560's theorem, PR968's floor 72 - p for masked decoders with exactly eight costly terms extends to p = 13 (floor 59, P107) and p = 14 (floor 58, P106). No kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop at P106 with every unit verified; P105, a structural (D)/(G) lemma and nine or more costly terms are left open.
evidence: verify.py --level 5: 11 exact checks (model and the frame identity (6) on all 2025 frames; generators; triple orbits; three-level candidate coverage with explicit generator words: 2517 quadruple candidates onto 180 representatives, 18782 5-subset candidates onto 1614 P107 units, 156627 6-subset candidates onto 19295 P106 units; PR1560's fixture and control; (G) and (D) each fail on deficient frame families of the fixture; a first-frame control; per P107 unit the pivot satisfies (D), (G), (W) and nonempty blocks, ranks modulo 1000003 as lower bounds). verify.py --level 6: the same per-unit checks on the 19295 P106 units. make_units.py checked that the orbit sizes sum to C(112,5) and C(112,6) (census, not needed by the argument). PR1560's Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 are cited; the author's assistant read the written proof and found no gap (not an independent human review). A read-only adversarial review by OpenAI Codex found no theorem-breaking issue; its one low-severity point (group order and orbit distinctness come from make_units.py) is reflected in the README. search_p105.py (unregistered, numpy float ranks) found a passing pivot for all 242802 P105 orbits, whose sizes sum to C(112,7); this is search evidence, not part of the verified result.

open_questions.question: Does every 7-subset of P112 (242802 orbits, P105) have a pivot satisfying PR1560's criterion, exactly verified?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would give floor 57 = 72 - 15 for masked eight-costly-term decoders on P105, the bottom of PR968's range.
open_questions.first_step: search_p105.py (numpy, float ranks) already finds a passing pivot for all 242802 orbits; next, make an exact stdlib replay affordable, e.g. (D) row certificates.
open_questions.blocked_by: A stdlib replay of about 2.4e5 units at about 25 ms each, plus about 1.65e6 coverage words, exceeds the registered 1200-second budget; needs a dedicated workflow or a structural (D)/(G) lemma.

open_questions.question: Do (D) and (G) hold at every pivot whenever enough live frames remain?
open_questions.why_it_matters: They never failed in the P107/P106 searches; a lemma would leave only the counting conditions (W) and nonempty blocks and remove the per-unit rank computations.
open_questions.first_step: Search for the smallest live sets where (D) or (G) fails at some pivot.
